blocks.content: Meghalaya's exceptionally high rainfall and forest cover (Chapters 1, 6) support a rich biodiversity profile, with several protected areas and community-led conservation models unique to the state's traditional land-tenure system.

cells: Known for its rugged canyon-and-plateau landscape, sometimes called the 'Land of Perpetual Winds'; culturally significant to the Garo, who consider it linked to their beliefs about the afterlife
UNESCO-designated Biosphere Reserve; important habitat for the red panda and the wild citrus species Citrus indica (believed to be the progenitor of many cultivated citrus varieties)
Notable birding site, also near significant limestone cave systems

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Nokrek National Park/Biosphere Reserve (West Garo Hills) is notable for hosting Citrus indica, believed by botanists to be the wild progenitor species from which many cultivated citrus fruits descend — a distinctive botanical-conservation fact for Meghalaya.

A distinctive feature of Meghalaya's environmental governance is the prevalence of privately and community-owned forests (clan forests, sacred groves, and village-council-managed forests), rather than the state-forest-department-dominated model found in most of India — a direct consequence of the state's traditional land-tenure system (linked to the Hima/Nokma institutions of Chapter 2), under which the majority of Meghalaya's forest land remains outside direct government ownership, making community consent and customary institutions central to conservation efforts in a way not typical of most Indian states.

items: Balpakram National Park (South Garo Hills) = culturally significant to the Garo, associated with afterlife beliefs.
Nokrek National Park/Biosphere Reserve (West Garo Hills) = UNESCO Biosphere Reserve; hosts Citrus indica, the believed wild ancestor of cultivated citrus fruits, and the red panda.
Most of Meghalaya's forest land is privately/community-owned (clan forests, sacred groves) rather than government-owned — a distinctive feature of the state's environmental governance.
